sentences.text: Diplodocus is easily recognized by its classic silhouette, featuring a very long neck and tail supported by four sturdy legs.
These massive reptiles held their bodies horizontally, with forelimbs noticeably shorter than their powerful hind legs.
Scientists estimate that a typical Diplodocus carnegii weighed between 12 and 14.8 metric tons.
Remarkably, the tail alone accounted for about 55 percent of the animal's total body length.
This giant could rear up onto its hind legs and tail to form a stable three-point stance, potentially reaching food 11 meters high.
Despite its enormous size, Diplodocus laid surprisingly small eggs and clutches.
It remains the most frequently depicted sauropod dinosaur, appearing in more museum displays than any other species.
The first fossils of this genus were unearthed in 1877.
Benjamin Mudge and Samuel Wendell Williston collected these initial remains at Garden Park near Cañon City, Colorado.
Othniel Charles Marsh formally named the genus Diplodocus in 1878.
Diplodocus is one of the best-studied dinosaurs because of the vast amount of skeletal material available to researchers.
The animal possessed highly unusual teeth with long, slender crowns that were elliptical in cross-section and ended in a blunt, triangular point.
Up to five replacement teeth were developing within each tooth socket at any given time.
Bone histology studies from the early 2000s suggested Diplodocus grew very fast and reached sexual maturity in just over a decade.
A 1992 study indicated that the longest-necked diplodocids would have required a heart weighing 1.6 tons, which is one-tenth of their body weight.
Researchers speculate that the tail may have served a defensive, noisemaking, or tactile function.
A 2011 study refuted the hypothesis that Diplodocus used its neck primarily for sexual display.
A 1951 study by Kenneth A. Kermack indicates sauropods likely could not breathe through nostrils while submerged due to water pressure.
The distribution of gastroliths found with a D. hallorum fossil suggests these animals may have had a digestive system similar to modern birds, with a crop and gizzard.
Diplodocus is the type genus and namesake of the family Diplodocidae.
The type species of Diplodocus is Diplodocus longus, which is considered a nomen dubium.
The Morrison Formation, where Diplodocus fossils are found, dates from 156.3 to 146.8 million years ago.
Diplodocus lived in what is now western North America during the Late Jurassic period.
Since the 1970s, the general consensus considers sauropods as firmly terrestrial animals, browsing among trees, ferns, and shrubs.
Sauropod footprints found in the 1930s disproved the theory that Diplodocus had a sprawling, lizard-like gait.
Matthew Cobley et al. (2013) disputed the idea that Diplodocus could feed from submerged plants, arguing that large muscles and cartilage limited neck movement.
